resources.string: To help delivery drivers, DashBuddy reads the screens of the delivery apps you turn on and reads offers aloud while you drive. Screen reading and calculations happen on your phone. Accept and Decline need your tap in DashBuddy; each automatic tap needs its own permission. If you allow Screen events, DashBuddy also sees which other app is open. It discards recognized screens with your banking, payment or ID details, or that photograph a document, before reading or saving their details. In test builds, saved screen text can include screens the filters missed, and uploading it needs switches in developer options. Optional screenshots save the whole screen; your gallery may sync them. Android backup may copy your history and settings.

DashBuddy reads the screens of the delivery apps you turn on. With Screen events on, it also sees which other app is open. It discards recognized screens with your banking, payment or ID details, or that photograph a document, before reading or saving their details. Screen reading and calculations happen on your phone. Customer names and addresses are saved as codes, not as text. Test builds can keep details the filters miss.

Automatic gas prices start off on a new install; an update keeps your setting. When on, Android's address lookup may send your location to its provider, and the U.S. Energy Information Administration gets a fuel-price request for your region. To stop it, set the bubble's gas price to manual.

Setup sends your vehicle to the EPA for MPG only after you tap "Look up my vehicle", and remembers that choice. Neither lookup sends an account or install ID. The manual MPG search opens Google with your vehicle.

Test builds only: census uploads need turning on in developer options, and trusted capture sharing can send customer text that the census server's operator can read. Regular builds do neither.

Optional screenshots of the whole screen go to Pictures/DashBuddy, where gallery sync may copy them. Android may back up your history and settings to your Google account or a new phone, and restore them later; consent records are left out. History, settings and test captures stay until you clear them or uninstall, logs keep only recent entries, and screenshots and exports stay until you delete them. More: Privacy details in Settings > Data & privacy > Automation & consent.

DashBuddy reads notifications only from the delivery apps you turn on, and skips other apps\' notifications unread. What it recognizes goes into your history, which Android backup may copy. Test builds can keep notification text, and their census sharing is off unless turned on. Regular builds can\'t upload it.
